work_packages.rework_note: Duplicate #resizer template variable causes incorrect element references in event handlers All three resizer elements — the new vertical one (inside .main__trees) and the two horizontal ones — share the same #resizer template reference variable within the same @if view scope. Previously the horizontal resizers didn't use inline (mousedown) bindings; instead viewChildren('resizer') collected them and ngAfterViewInit attached listeners via Renderer2. That approach worked fine with duplicate names. Now that all three use inline (mousedown)="onResizerMouseDown($event, resizer)", Angular resolves the resizer identifier against the view's local variable context, which is overwritten each time an element with #resizer is encountered during rendering. This means all three event handlers end up passing the last-declared #resizer element (the second horizontal resizer) as the resizer argument, breaking the getAdjacentPanels lookup for the first two. Give each resizer a unique template variable name:

Huge bug!! Three elements in the same template scope all declare #resizer (lines 25, 59, 81). Angular template variable names must be unique within a view; duplicate names shadow each other and can cause subtle resolution issues with static analysis tools and future Angular compiler changes. Each separator already has a unique data-testid and CSS modifier — give each a distinct template reference variable instead:

<!-- vertical separator inside .main__trees -->
#verticalResizer   (mousedown)="onResizerMouseDown($event, verticalResizer)"

<!-- first horizontal separator -->
#leftResizer       (mousedown)="onResizerMouseDown($event, leftResizer)"

<!-- second horizontal separator -->
#rightResizer      (mousedown)="onResizerMouseDown($event, rightResizer)"

findings.summary: treeHeightResizerAriaValues starts at a hardcoded default (min:180, now:180, max:360) and is only recomputed on focus or drag start (onTreeHeightResizerFocus / onResizerMouseDown / startDrag). If a screen-reader user reaches the separator via any path that does not fire a focus event, or if actual rendered panel heights differ from the 2x-min assumption before first interaction, aria-valuenow/aria-valuemax could be briefly inaccurate. No user-visible resize failure results; this is an ARIA-freshness gap, not a broken resize.

In the 'should use vertical cursor movement for tree panel height resizers' unit test, left/right getBoundingClientRect mocks only stub width ({width:400}/{width:600} as DOMRect), so the axis='y' code path in onResizerMouseDown reads rect.height as undefined when syncTreeHeightResizerAriaValues runs before the (separately stubbed) startDrag call. This produces NaN aria values silently rather than a test failure; harmless today because the test doesn't assert on aria state, but the mock doesn't reflect real vertical geometry.
